title: Adaptable toolbox to characterize Alzheimer’s disease pathology in mouse models
protocol: Anesthetize the mouse with IP injection of 100 mg/kg Ketamine and 1 mg/kg Xylazine in accordance with IACUC guidelines.
Sanitize and prepare the chest and abdomen area with 70% ethanol.

Pinch the abdominal skin with rat tooth forceps to make a small incision upward through the skin and peritoneum, then cut parallel through the diaphragm, then parallel to the body through the ribs to just above the heart.
Gently push down the liver with the side of scissors while cutting to avoid nicking it and the lung.
Cut away the connective tissue around the heart for full display.
Clamp the sternum/rib with hemostats to open the rib cage.
Nick the right atrium gently.
Inject needle tip laterally into left ventricle at an upward 20-degree angle toward the midline.
Perfuse for 30 s-1 min with PBS/Heparin at a speed of 0.3 mL/s at 37°C if followed by PFA fixation.
Alternatively, perfuse with ice-cold D-PBS for a total of 2 minutes if collecting fresh brains.
Monitor liver color change from dark red to pale mustard as an indicator of good perfusion.
Note the angle of the needle and observe the liver changing color over time.
If collecting fresh brains, proceed to step 35 for “Isolation of soluble Aβ from transgenic AD mouse cortex and hippocampus and its measurement by sandwich ELISA”.
Otherwise, perfuse with 4% PFA/PBS for 5 min at 37°C or room temperature.
Make an incision down the midline to tease apart the skin of the head.
Gently nick and peel away the skull bone using bone scissors starting from the cerebellum and brainstem.
Place the dissected whole brain into the acrylic mouse brain matrix.
Align with symmetry and slice down the midline with a clean razor blade to separate the two hemispheres.
Place two hemispheres on a petridish on ice lined with a filter paper pre-wetted with PBS.
Immerse the dissected brain hemispheres into a glass vial filled with at least 10 mL of 4% PFA in PBS for fixation overnight at 4°C.
Switch to 30% sucrose/PBS (at least 10 mL per brain) to infiltrate overnight at 4°C.
Fill the foil mold to 90% fullness with TFM.
Customize tissue freezing molds using foil of tissue-fitted sizes.
Avoid bubbles in the molds.
Fish out bubbles if any, using tweezer tips or pipette tips.
Fill a glass petri dish with 20–30 mL of isopentane and set on dry ice to cool down.
Drop a chuck of dry ice into isopentane to speed up cooling.
Blot surfaces of brain hemispheres thoroughly using Kimwipe tissues after picking them up from sucrose.
Pick up the brain gently using curved tweezers, guide it all the way to the bottom of the foil molds with the flat midline side facing down until adherence.
Cryosection mouse brain tissue blocks at -25°C.
Label microscopy slides with permanent markers or pencil.
Trim frozen block starting from the midline where the hippocampus begins to be fully shown, from approximately 0.25 mm–0.85 mm from the midline, each spaced 0.15 mm apart.
Use a thin art brush to guide the TFM bottom edge of a section downward to obtain a flat and smooth surface.
Add one drop of water on the desired location on the slide.
Grab the medium part of the section with a pre-chilled fine tip tweezer.
Place the section gently and flat on top of the water drop in the cryostat.
Use a small transfer pipette to suck away the residual water underneath the section until it adheres flat onto the slide.
Air-dry slides at room temperature overnight.
Store slides at −80°C for future use or use immediately for immunofluorescence experiments.
Re-seal unfinished frozen TFM tissue blocks by applying a thin layer of TFM at the cut surface.
Store resealed tissue blocks at −80°C in airtight containers for reuse.
Thaw TFM tissue blocks stored at -80°C in room temperature for 10 minutes.
Ensure cryosections are completely dry on the slides and free from extra mounting medium to ensure proper adhesion.
Perform ThioS staining if applicable.
Prepare 70% ethanol solution, 400 mL.
Prepare 80% ethanol solution, 600 mL.
Make fresh 0.1% ThioS solution in 200 mL of 80% ethanol and filter through 0.22 μm filter.
Wash slides with 70% ethanol for 1 min.
Wash slides with 80% ethanol for 1 min.
Incubate slides in filtered thioflavin S solution for 15 min in dark.
Wash slides with 80% ethanol for 1 min in dark.
Wash slides with 70% ethanol for 1 min in dark.
Wash slides with distilled water twice before mounting.
Wash slides with 1×PBS for 5 min.
Preheat citrate-based antigen retrieval (AR) buffer to ∼60°C–70°C.
Transfer the slides from PBS buffer and immerse into the pre-warmed AR buffer.
Microwave the AR jar for 2 min on power 10 to reach a temperature of 80°C–90°C.
Rinse and wash the slides once with PBST for 5 min after cooling.
Prepare PBS-T (wash buffer) by adding 1 mL of Tween-20 to 1,000 mL PBS.
Prepare a humidified chamber ("immunobox") using wet tissue paper to prevent evaporation during incubation.
Use a hydro-barrier PAP pen to draw edges on the glass slides.
Wait one minute before adding blocking buffer (BB) to each sagittal brain section.
Incubate slides in immunobox at room temperature for 1 h.
Make primary antibody mixture in BB, estimating ∼100 μL solution for each brain section.
Incubate slides in primary antibody mixture in a humidified chamber overnight at 4°C in the dark.
Spin down antibodies at maximum speed on a tabletop centrifuge for 30 seconds to remove precipitated antibodies.
Rinse and wash slides with wash buffer for 3 times, each time for 10 minutes.
Prepare secondary antibody mixture by diluting in blocking buffer (BB) depending on the optic setup of the confocal microscope (e.g., Alexa Fluor 488 and 546 or Alexa Fluor 647 at a 1:500 dilution).
Spin down antibodies at maximum speed on a tabletop centrifuge and withdraw from the top to avoid fluorescent antibody precipitates.
Incubate sections with TrueBlack (20×) or Sudan Black D (0.1%) dissolved in 70% EtOH for 1 minute before rinsing in PBS for 5 minutes if autofluorescence quenching is necessary.
After autofluorescence quenching, use PBS instead of wash buffer and non-detergent-containing blocking buffer in subsequent steps.
Incubate section in secondaries at room temperature in the dark.
Prepare Hoechst33258 solution for nuclei staining: Dilute 1% Bis Benzamide stock solution 1:1000 in PBS.
Alternatively, use DAPI-containing mounting media at the end of the process.
Suck off the secondaries with a vacuum suction system and incubate in Hoechst solution for 5 minutes at room temperature in the dark.
Rinse sections three times for 10 minutes each with wash buffer.
Wash sections once with PBS.
Wash sections once with distilled water.
Apply approximately 20 μL of Fluoromount-G per section or 50 μL to cover the whole slide.
Gently lay down the coverslip using fine point tweezers from one side to the other carefully to avoid bubbles.
If small bubbles form, use a pipet tip to gently tap near the bubble on the cover glass to drive out any bubbles.
Optional: apply mounting medium to coverslips instead of onto sections (∼60 μL per 50 mm long coverslip) for efficient mounting and bubble formation prevention.
Alternatively, mount coverslips into Vectashield mounting medium with DAPI or ProLong Gold antifade mountant with DAPI onto glass slides.
Store slides at room temperature in a dry and dark place overnight before imaging.
Store mounted slides at 4°C.
Transfer the perfused brain to a dry filter paper and quickly roll a full round to roughly remove the meningeal layer.
Place the brain onto a D-PBS-wetted filter paper on an ice-cooled petri dish.
Dissociate hippocampus and cortex from the perfused brain.
Use a clean razor blade to slice down the midline of the brain on ice.
Tease away brainstem, cerebellum, olfactory bulb, and other subcortical parenchyma using the rounded edge of a spatula.
Place the two halves of cortex down and use iris micro-scissors and the tip of the curved spatula to gently tease outward the crescent-shaped hippocampus without protruding into the cortex.
Trim as much white matter as possible with micro-scissors to yield the cortex.
Snap freeze dissected tissues in liquid nitrogen for storage at −80°C or proceed immediately with homogenization on ice.
Add 500 μL of ice-cold lysis buffer (RIPA + Halt protease and phosphatase inhibitor cocktail) to each hemisphere of cortical samples.
Add 250 μL of lysis buffer to each pooled bilateral hippocampal sample.
Homogenize tissue in lysis buffer using a motorized pestle for 30 seconds on ice.
Set homogenate on ice and agitate every five minutes by vortexing briefly.
Spin down the sample for 5 minutes at 16,000 g (12,000 rpm) at 4°C.
Transfer 200 μl of supernatant to ultracentrifuge tubes chilled on ice; discard debris.
Store remaining supernatant lysate at -80°C for immunoblotting assays.
Centrifuge the samples at 4°C for 1 hour at 100,000 g (or 55,000 rpm).
Pre-chill rotor to 4°C in ultracentrifuge before use; set up speed and program on the ultracentrifuge.
Weigh tubes beforehand to balance for ultracentrifugation.
Set up BCA assay according to manufacturer’s instructions.
Calculate respective concentration of each supernatant sample before and after ultracentrifugation with a dilution factor of 10 and 2, respectively.
Aliquot the supernatant to the prepared tubes.
Parafilm seal the pellet in the polycarbonate tubes for further extraction of insoluble Aβ.
Freeze the supernatant and pellet tubes in −80°C or at −20°C for ELISA the next day.
Dilute human Aβ42 capture antibodies (Aβ 42: JRF A042/26, Janssen Pharmaceutica) to a final concentration of capture antibody = 1.5 μg/mL.
Load 50 μL of solution each well in one 96-well transparent flat-bottom plate.
Incubate overnight on shake at 4°C, covered with plate seal to avoid evaporation.
Wash plate 5× with 150 μL of ELISA wash buffer per well.
Add 50 μL of 1% casein blocking buffer to block and incubate in RT for 3 h.
Prepare the serial dilution for one plate with eight Aβ42 standards in duplicates (31.25–2,000 pg/mL).
Mix samples using a round bottom 96 well plate; label plate if needed.
For each 12 mo. cortex sample from APP/PS1 mice, dilute 6 μL of supernatant sample in 54 μL of casein blocking buffer for a 1:10 dilution.
For each 12 mo. hippocampus sample from APP/PS1 mice, dilute 15 μL of supernatant sample in 45 μL of casein blocking buffer for a 1:4 dilution.
Wash 5× with PBS + 0.05% Tween-20.
Load 25 μL of standard dilution #1–8 and 25 μL of samples, both in duplicates.
Prepare a 1/2000 dilution of N25-biotinylated human antibody in casein blocking buffer for a final concentration = 1.07 μg/mL.
Add 25 μL of the diluted antibody to each well on top of standards and samples.
Incubate overnight at 4°C.
Wash wells 5× with ELISA wash buffer.
Prepare a 1:2500 dilution of streptavidin-HRP for 50 μL/well, mixing 2.5 μL diluted in 5 mL BB.
Incubate the plate for 30 min.
Wash wells 5× with ELISA wash buffer.
Prepare substrate right before the last wash by mixing 1:1 Color Reagent A (H2O2) and Color Reagent B (Tetramethylbenzidine).
Load 50 μL of substrate into each well immediately after preparation.
Incubate in the dark for 15 min or until color fully develops.
Add 50 μL of stop solution (H2SO4) to each well.
Measure plates on a TECAN Infinite® 200 PRO reader at 450 nm within 30 min of adding the stop solution.
